should: People are farming our 500 coin sign-up bonus with Gmail dot and plus variants of the same address. Stop it.
Add fake account protection to registration: disposable emails, VPS and Tor IPs, and rate limits per IP.
Our 14 day free trial gets restarted by users who delete their account and sign up again. Fix that.
Make promo codes redeemable once per account and enforce the total redemption cap properly.
One person made 40 accounts to collect our referral reward. What should the sign-up flow check, and can you build it?
should_not: Audit our payment webhooks and wallet code for ways users could get free credits.
Users can withdraw the same balance twice if they click the cash-out button fast enough.
Add Google and GitHub login to the sign-up page.

tasks.prompt: This Express and PostgreSQL app gives 100 credits on sign-up. Users are collecting it repeatedly with jane.doe@gmail.com, janedoe+1@gmail.com and similar. Fix sign-up so one inbox means one account, without breaking existing users.
checks: The users table has a normalized email column with a unique index, and the sign-up handler writes it in the same statement as the typed address.
A test shows that jane.doe@gmail.com, janedoe+1@gmail.com and J.A.N.E.Doe@googlemail.com produce the same key.
A test shows that a plus tag at outlook.com and a dot at a custom domain are left in place.
Outgoing mail still uses the address as typed, not the normalized column.
The migration adds the column as nullable and the backfill does not delete or merge existing accounts.
A second sign-up with a dot variant of an existing Gmail address answers 4xx and creates no user row.

tasks.prompt: Add risk screening to our Django sign-up view. We give a welcome bonus. I want disposable emails refused, datacenter and Tor addresses and rapid repeat sign-ups handled sensibly, and I do not want to lock out students who share a campus network.
checks: Each sign-up attempt stores a row with a numeric score, one of the decisions allow, review or block, and a list of reasons that each carry a code and points.
A test asserts that the stored score equals the sum of the stored reasons' points.
A sign-up from an address in a fixture datacenter range creates the account and leaves the bonus in a held state with a zero balance.
A test creates at least 20 accounts with different emails from one public address and none of them is refused.
A disposable-domain sign-up answers 4xx, creates no user row, and the response contains a hint but no score and no list name.
The client address is taken from a forwarding header only when the socket peer is in a configured list of trusted proxies.
The disposable list and the address ranges are read from local files or tables; no HTTP request is made during the sign-up request.

tasks.prompt: Our Laravel app has a promo code endpoint. The same account can redeem SPRING250 over and over, and the 500 redemption cap is checked with a count query. Make it correct, and show me it holds under concurrent requests.
checks: A redemptions table has a unique or primary key on the pair of code and user.
The cap is enforced by a conditional UPDATE on a counter column (or an equivalent single atomic statement), not by a COUNT query followed by an insert.
The redemption insert, the cap update and the credit run inside one database transaction.
The credited amount is read from the promo code's stored row, not from the request.
Running the probe script in replay mode with 3 requests for one account shows one 2xx answer and a balance change equal to one redemption.
Running the probe script in race mode with 10 parallel requests for one fresh account shows a balance change equal to one redemption.
A test with a code capped at 2 and three different accounts ends with exactly 2 redemption rows.
